# Review (pass 1) — hammurabi-epilogue-3 (Col. XLII 98 – XLIII 80)

Reviewer: adversarial pass 1. `units.json` edited in place by script (json load/modify/dump, `ensure_ascii=False`, indent 1; the untouched file round-trips byte-identically; the pre-edit copy is in the session scratchpad only). `python3 ../run3/signs.py check`: in sync (no sign added or changed). Nothing committed, built or published; no file touched but `units.json` and this one.

## Counts

Edits (one entry per field changed): **36** — high 4, medium 10, low 22. Distinct findings: about 22 (several entries are one finding touching `l`/`i`/note/`say` together). No finding blocks the build; one open question for the lead (F1, the ḫal key in the published parts) and one carried (F2, XLIII 70–74 division).

## What I did on the plates

Method: Harper's plates 78–80 (PDF pp. 371, 373, 375) rendered at zoom 3–9 with `page.py` and my own crops; rows counted against Harper's numerals (the numerals sit in the lower part of their row, and a sub-row such as XLIII 30 or 45 shifts the count — I counted from the identified rows, not the labels alone); Harper's List of Signs pp. 383 (no. 1–11), 391 (59–71), 393 (73–94), 397 (108–121), 401 (126–137), 403 (138–148), 405 (149–161), 411 (203–209); Harper's glossary text layer (PDF pp. 165–215) for every entry cited in the notes. I did **not** open PDF p. 125 or any modern translation. (Harper's glossary glosses, e.g. sakâru "to dam up", šêrtu "sword, scimitar", are lexical aids and were read as such.)

**Confirmed on the plate:**
- **Line division, whole part.** Plate 78 (XLII 98 … 103, XLIII 1 … 25) rows: 98 star+EN.KI row, 100 labelled row, 101 abkal ilī (big wedges), 102 the full-width row, 103 four widely spaced signs, then the column heading and XLIII 1–2. Plate 79 rows 25–48 and 48–72, plate 80 rows 73–: every unit's first line falls on the row that carries its words (spot-checked: 25 li-iš-ḫi-[el]-ṣi with the dotted [el]; 27 the UZU row; 28/29 the SUḪUŠ row; 30 two tiers (the second starts with LI); 39 two big signs + šu; 45 tall two-tier row; 46, 47; 50; 52; 65–75). The mechanical check (85 source lines against the units' `nl` breaks, by script) gives 85 = 85, no word-count difference except XLIII 52 (Harper prints arḫi twice; the unit has one ITI.ITI word, see below).
- **XLIII 70–74.** Plate 79 bottom / plate 80 top: row 70 i-na na-ak-bi-im (label 70 on it), 71 li-te-ir-šu (four groups), **72 two signs only, one at each end (ma-zu)**, 73 i-na ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im (seven signs), 74 u bu-bu-tim, 75 li-ḫal-li-iq (label 75). The drafter's note is right: five ruled rows between the numerals. The unit keeps Harper's four-segment division (72 ma-zu ina ḫušaḫḫim / 73 u bubūtim / 75), as epilogue-2 did for XLII 5–9 (QUESTIONS.md, 2026-10-15); nothing to change in the unit; the display will show ma-zu i-na ḫu-ša-aḫ-ḫi-im on one line where the stone has two. Same open point as in epilogue-2 (amend the pinned source, then `nl` at ina and u would move).
- **ḫal (the lead's check).** Harper's List no. 2 (ḫal) = a horizontal wedge crossed by an X; no. 159 (ḫar, mur) = a hatched diamond + wedge (Unicode HI×ASH₂). Plate rows XLIII 75 (li-ḫal-li-iq: LI, X-wedge, LI, IQ) and XLIII 50 (la i-ḫal-li-qu) carry the X-wedge: the key is **HAL**, not HAR. Fixed (4 entries below; HIGH).
- **XLIII 45 agâm kussâm.** Row 45 is a tall two-tier row; upper tier = four sign-groups (a bar-with-hatch-and-upright, then a plain GIŠ-shape, a small triangle with a wedge, a chevron-and-hatch), lower tier = ša šar-ru-tim. Harper's glossary: "AGÛ, crown [MIR]: 43, 45; a-gi-im, 3, 26" (so at 43, 45 it is a Sumerogram; the syllabic spelling is the litany's) and "KUSSÛ, seat, throne [IŠ.GU.ZA]: 6, 24, 43, 45". The drafter's six signs (a-ga-am + three) do not fit four groups; one logogram + GIŠ.GU.ZA does. Rebuilt (HIGH), marked TENTATIVE. The first group has the outline of the first sign of List no. 135 (agû / rid-ṣâbê = AGA₃.ÚS, the key GIN2 = Unicode DUN3 GUNU GUNU used for AGA₃.ÚS in laws-26-41); I could not do better than outline.
- **UZU (XLIII 27).** Row 27 = hatched group + diamond-with-arrow (together one sign, as in List no. 80 šêru/šîru: a hatched part + a diamond-and-arrow part), then IGI (lim) and NAM. Drafter's UZU stands (TENTATIVE, as the sign note says).
- **GIDIM (XLIII 39).** Row 39 = two large identical signs + šu at the right; List no. 203 ekimmu is one sign of that look. GEKIM.GEKIM = GIDIM.GIDIM-šu stands (TENTATIVE).
- **ÍD.ÍD (XLIII 7).** Two groups each of an A-shape + a boxed hatched part, + šu: stands. **ŠE.TIR (XLIII 11).** Star, ŠE (chevron stack), TIR (chevron stack + hatch; List no. 145 tir; List no. 142 shows ašnan as star + ŠE + TIR-like): stands. **ITI.ITI (XLIII 52).** UD, MI, then two boxed chevron signs: the doubled ITI is on the plate; one word arḫī is right.
- **Sumerograms' `val`/`say`:** {d}EN.KI Ea, NUN rubûm, NUN.ME abkal, NI.NI ilī, ÍD.ÍD nārāt-, {d}ŠE.TIR Ašnan, {d}UTU Šamaš, SUḪUŠ išid (3 ×), UZU šīram, GIDIM.GIDIM ekimmê, {d}EN.ZU Sîn, DINGIR ilum, {giš}GU.ZA kussâm (kuss/ê-style split as laws-1-10), UD-um/UD-mi, ITI.ITI, BALA-šu palêšu, ḪÉ.GÁL-im ḫegallim, {d}IM Adad, URU-šu ālišu: all checked against the glossary / earlier parts; `reading` rebuilt from the glyph `tr` for all 21 units by script: no mismatch; morph indices cover the glyphs for all words (before and after my edits); no ḳ anywhere (reader-facing fields, notes included).

**Not done:** every syllabogram of all 85 lines was not matched shape by shape against the List of Signs. I counted sign-groups per row for the lines named above and spot-checked recurring signs (LI, ŠU, TIM, NA, I, ZU, LA, BA, IR); the rest of the readings rest on Harper's transliteration, the group counts and the drafter's own plate reading. I could not tell GU/ZA apart from their neighbours in line 45 (only outline). I did not verify the GUL (kul) sign shape of tu-kul-ti, the AK / IG / KAB / KU values, or the dotted [el] at the glyph level beyond seeing the dotted group.

### Full text of the three long note rewrites

**#5 n (bēlum tukulti):** now reads `bēlum tukulti is read “the lord, my trust”, UNCERTAIN: the title stands alone after the string of epithets. be-lum is the full nominative, not the construct bēl that this text writes in be-el šamê (xliii 41) and be-el ḫegallim (xliii 64), so it does not govern tukulti; and the other gods’ epithets close the same way, with a “my” noun (ilum bānî “the god, my creator”, rēṣūa “my helper”), so tu-kul-ti is taken as tukultī, the suffix -ī not written out. The alternative, the construct chain bēl tukulti “lord of trust”, is possible if the -um is a slip. tukultu is Harper’s “strength” (his glossary has tu-kul-ti at this line, without a suffix), modern “support, reliance”; “trust” is my choice; the GUL sign is read kul (Harper’s list no. 164).`

**#12 n (the signs):** replaces the drafter's "I read agâm as the syllabic a-ga-am … which I could not match one for one with these six signs" with the glossary evidence and the four-group count (see HIGH entry above and "What I did on the plates").

**#3 n:** adds the tarûm possibility (LOW) and Harper's "to dam up" as his gloss.

## Findings refused (with reason)

- **"evil omen" (#7) as stock phrase, kept in `l` as "evil".** Partly accepted: `i` is now "a bad omen" and the surrounding phrase rebuilt; `l` keeps "evil" (the glossary word for lemnum; epilogue-2 uses "evil" for the same adjective). Without the lead's flag I would have left "evil omen" as the plain consequence of the grammar; the change is cosmetic and can be reverted.
- **"great judge of heaven and earth", "grievous word", "uproot", "overthrow his kingship", "destroy the foundation of his army", "a mound of the flood", "bring … to an end", "the equal of death", "decree for him as his fate", "regent of heaven and earth", "storm":** all read for remembered phrasing; each is a plain consequence of the grammar and Harper's glossary glosses (dajjānum rabûm, awātum marūštum, nasāḫum (house: uproot), sakāpu "to overthrow", išid ummānišu, tīl abūbim, qatû III,1, šanānu, ana šīmtim lišīmšum (house), gugallu "regent"). Left. "who knows everything there is" (#1) is the litany's own house phrase (mimma šumšu). Nothing in `i` matched a distinctive modern sentence I recognise beyond those I changed.
- **litēršu / litēr as "D precative of târum" (#2, #12, #17, #20).** The li- + D shape is unusual (a D precative is lu-; litūr would be G), but epilogue-2 fixed the form and the rendering ("let him turn away from him", conventions: "`litēršu` recurs in later epilogue parts — render the same way"). Not relitigated; flagged for the lead only as a known soft spot.
- **li-iš-ḫi-el-ṣi, li-mu-zu-ma, li-it-ta-ar-ru-šu, ši-ta-an-nu, li-ši, li-is-si-ma (#3, #6, #13, #15, #19):** the stem labels (Š of ḫalāṣum, "D" of emēdum, Gt of târum, Gt of šanānum, ešûm, nisûm) are Harper's and several are unlikely in modern Akkadian (limussuma, as the note itself says, looks like a G precative of emēdum: limud-šu-ma); the notes already say UNCERTAIN. I could not improve them from the grammar and Harper's glossary alone, so I left them, with the notes' existing hedge.
- **šīmātūšu (#0) long ū before -šu:** I could not settle whether the fem. plural nominative + -šu is šīmātušu or šīmātūšu from the repository; left as drafted, spelled as Harper's ši-ma-tu-šu.
- **The `nl` flag / line-break display at XLIII 72–75 (#18):** left as drafted (follows the pinned source, as epilogue-2 did); see the plate confirmation above.
- **Harper's [el] bracket in `reading` ("li-iš-ḫi-[el]-ṣi") and `tr` "[el]":** left as drafted; it matches the pinned source's bracketing; if the build rejects bracketed `tr`, that is a build matter.
- **Sign `tr` "zu" for the ZU in ri-zu-u-a, ma-zu, šar-ru-zu, še-ri-zu, li-ik-šu-zu, li-mu-zu-ma:** left; the `reading` is Harper's spelling and `say` carries ṣu/ssu (as epilogue-2).

## Open points for the lead

- **F1 (ḫal key in the published parts).** HAR is used with `tr` "ḫal" in published laws-1-10 (2 glyphs), laws-11-25 (4), laws-112-126 (3), laws-215-240 (4); only laws-52-65 uses HAL. By the plate and List no. 2/159 these are probably HAL as well (I checked only this part's two). Not touched here (published parts, other works' files). The sign glossary entry for HAL says "in u-ḫal-li-qu (§53)"; HAR says "ḫar/ḫur in ḪAR.SAG.KALAM.MA".
- **F2 (XLIII 70–74).** As XLII 5–9 in epilogue-2: plate = five rows, source = four segments; QUESTIONS.md already carries it.
- **Glosser must know:** (a) `agûm` already has the litany entry "crown"; broaden with "written with the one logogram AGA₃ at XLIII 45 (xliii 45, TENTATIVE sign), syllabic a-gi-im in the litany". (b) `balṭum`: form balṭūtim (ina balṭūtim, "among the living"), spelled ba-al-tu-tim with TU for ṭu. (c) `tukultum`: tukultī "my trust" (apposition after bēlum, UNCERTAIN), Harper's "strength". (d) `sekērum`: "to shut off, block" (Harper: "to dam up"). (e) `šadālum`: broaden with lišaddilšu "(let him) extend, increase" (D, Harper II,1; the litany's mušaddil "who widens"). (f) `Ašnan`: the grain-deity (a goddess in modern accounts), written {d}ŠE.TIR. (g) New lemmas, check each against the text: maḫrum, abkallum, arākum-Š (mušarriku), mišītum, nārum (ÍD.ÍD, doubled sign = plural), sekērum, Ašnan, ešērum-Št (muštēšir), tukultum, sakāpum, urḫum, ešûm, ummānum, ḫalāṣum-Š, bīrum, lemnum, marūštum, arḫiš, balṭum, ekimmum (GIDIM.GIDIM, plural by doubling), zamûm-Š, šērtum ("sword", Harper's second noun) and šērtum-sin ("sin"), kammalum, dimmatum, qatûm-Š, gugallum, zunnum, mīlum, bubūtum, izzum, nisûm, tīlum, abūbum, plus bašûm-Š / ḫalāqum / ḫalāqum-D / šanānum / diānum etc. already in earlier glossaries. Existing `ḫalāqum` entry (laws-215-240) is "to be lost, vanish" — covers iḫalliqu (lā iḫalliqu "will not vanish"); `ḫalāqum-D` covers liḫalliq. (h) Sonnet will probably name `lišaddilšu`, `lišaqti`, `lišḫelṣi` stems loosely: they are D, Š and Š precatives (li-) as the notes say.
- The part's signs: UZU, GIDIM were added by the drafter with TENTATIVE notes; HAL is an existing key; GIN2 (AGA₃) is an existing key.

# Pass 2 — hammurabi-epilogue-3 (gloss.json, lemma keys, units.json re-skim)

Reviewer: adversarial pass 2. Edited `units.json`, `gloss.json` and `newlemmas.json` in place by script (json load/modify/dump, `ensure_ascii=False`, indent 1). Nothing built, published or committed. Harper's glossary was read from the PDF text layer (PDF pp. 165–216; p. 125 and every translation unopened) and the page image of BÛBÛTU was checked at the glyph level. No ḳ anywhere (grep on `units.json`, `gloss.json`).

## Counts
Edits: **17** — high 0, medium 5, low 12. Open: 2 (below).

## Checks that passed
- **Keys.** 35 new gloss keys = the 35 lemmas of `newlemmas.json`, all used in `units.json`, none already in a published glossary; every lemma used but neither new nor broadened (47 of them) is in an earlier part's glossary, and the old entries cover the forms used (checked by script: each `say`/`reading` found in the old entry, or the entry is general: -šu, u, ša, ina …; hand-checked rabûm fem., šīmtum pl., rubûm, ḫegallum, rēṣum). Every lemma in each unit's `morph` has a gloss key; `__broaden__` (26) keys all exist in earlier glossaries and are all used.
- **Stems against Harper's glossary:** mušarriku = ARÂKU III,1 (Š; II,1 li-ir-ri-ik is D); lišaddilšu = ŠADÂLU II,1 (D; the li-ša-ad-di-il shape is li + D šaddil, not a Š; Harper "to extend, to multiply"; mušaddil, 3, 18, same verb); lišaqti = KATÛ (qatû) III,1 (Š); lišḫelṣi = ḪALṢU III,1 "to destroy" (Š); lišazmi = ZAMÛ III,1 "to deprive" (Š); liskir, liskip = SAKÂRU I,1 "to dam up", SAKÂPU I,1 "to overthrow" (G precatives); muštēšir = ešēru III,2 (Št, with šutēšurum); littarrūšu = TÂRU I,2 (Gt-shape, uncertain); litēr, litēršu = TÂRU II,1 (D, soft spot kept from epilogue-2); šitannu = ŠANÂNU I,2; limussuma = EMÊDU II,1; lissima = NISÛ I,1; liši = EŠÛ I,1 "to confuse, cause to err"; lišīmšum = ŠÂMU I,1 "to decree". Meanings of maḫru, abkallu, bīru, urḫu, tukultu "strength", marūštu "blighting", ummānu, kammalu, dimmatu, gugallu, zunnu, mīlu "water-flood", telu "hill, heap", zumru, mišîtu, ekimmu (Harper normalizes ekimmê-šu), BÛBÛTU, ašnan: as Harper.

## Refused / left
- ARÂKU: Harper's III,1 mu-ša-ri-ku is kept as Š participle; the final -u (construct with nominative vowel) is the drafter's explanation, as for mušarbû; left, already hedged by being parallel to the published form.
- littarrūšu, limussuma, liši, lišḫelṣi, litēr/litēršu, šitannu: stem labels are Harper's; modern grammar doubts are already marked UNCERTAIN in notes and glosses.
- šērissu (še-ri-zu): the vowel of šērissu from šērtum + -šu is not explained anywhere in the repository; left.
- "who knows everything there is", "the equal of death": plain grammar renderings; left.

## Open
- F1 (ḫal key HAR vs HAL in earlier published parts) and F2 (XLIII 70–74 divider) from pass 1 stay with the lead.
- šērissu: two Harper nouns of one spelling; which one the Sîn curse at xliii 43 means is Harper's, not independent.
